html:
Under Sultan Bolkiah, who reigned around 1485 to 1524, Brunei reached the height of its power. Its influence stretched along the coasts of Borneo and north into the Sulu islands and to Manila.

After the Portuguese took Malacca in 1511 (see Portugal takes Malacca), Muslim traders moved to other ports, and Brunei gained. Bolkiah is remembered as a sailor king who led fleets himself.

When Magellan's surviving ships called in 1521, Pigafetta described a great town built over water, the Kampong Ayer. Spanish expansion from Manila soon cut Brunei's reach, leading to the Castilian War.
